arm-A.title: The Bug Extraction
arm-A.summary: In the moving car, Neo is made to strip and lie back while Trinity seals an extraction device over his navel and Switch feeds it power from the cigarette lighter. Told he is bugged, Neo endures the machine sucking at his stomach and, when the ultrasound monitor shows the parasite shifting, Trinity escalates to an electric charge that convulses him until the bug is driven out through the coils. She displays the writhing thing in a glass cage, then rolls down the window and drops it; it hits the pavement and reverts into an ordinary wire tap as the vehicle drives off into the wet darkness.

arm-B.title: The Bug Removed
arm-B.summary: In the car rushing through the rainy night, Trinity seals an extractor over Neo's navel and, when suction alone fails to catch the burrowing tracker, overrides his screams and electrocutes him until the fluke-like bug is driven out through the coils. Neo, who had feared only a wire tap, is stunned into belief when he sees the living thing writhing in the glass cage, and Trinity empties it out into the downpour. The car carries them on through the wet night and comes to a halt in the deserted alley behind Hotel Lafayette.
arm-B.action: Trinity fits the extraction device to Neo's stomach and raises the suction while Switch feeds it power from the cigarette lighter; as the ultrasound monitor shows the tracker burrowing and Switch warns it will be lost, Trinity fires an electric charge through Neo, convulsing him until the bug rockets out into the glass cage, which she then empties out the window. The car drives on through the wet night and stops in the alley behind Hotel Lafayette.

arm-A.title: Waking in the Pod and Recovery
arm-A.summary: Neo breaks out of his pod and grasps that he and countless others are farmed in pods, only to be disconnected by a machine and sucked into a black hole; he is then flushed through waste lines until he nearly drowns, is hauled by a cable into a flying machine, and is lowered half-conscious into a hovercraft where Morpheus names him and the real world before he passes out.
arm-A.action: Neo breaks free of the gelatin shroud, recognizes himself as Neo and sees the endless ranks of other farmed bodies, and is seized by a machine that unlocks and unplugs him before a vacuum drags him into a black hole. He falls and slides through a waste pipe, is flushed up through grease traps, nearly drowns in the sewer main, and is snatched from the flow by a metallic cable into a hovering flying machine. Inside the hovercraft the harness opens, human hands lift him up, and Morpheus names him and welcomes him to the real world before he collapses.

arm-B.title: Born Into the Real World
arm-B.summary: Neo tears free of the magenta pod, bald and naked and sight-blurred, and is carried through the body's waste channels after a machine seizes him, unlocks the coaxial cable from the base of his skull, and frees the connective hoses from his limbs and genitals before dropping him into a black hole that vacuums him into the waste line. He slides and nearly drowns in the flow until a metallic cable snatches him up into a flying machine, which carries him into the hovercraft and lowers him, half-conscious, onto its floor. Morpheus names him and the real world, and Neo, emptied by the passage, gives out and collapses.

arm-A.title: The Construct and the Desert of the Real
arm-A.summary: Morpheus jacks Neo into the Construct and, over a guided descent through the history of the war and the horror of the human battery farms, lays out the full truth of the Matrix; Neo's mind refuses to take it in and his body violently ejects him back to the ship, where he collapses.
arm-A.action: On the main deck, Morpheus has Trinity seat Neo in one of the six ecto-skeleton chairs and feeds a coaxial cable into the socket at the rear of Neo's neck until a CLICK fires and Neo drops into weightlessness. He wakes in the blank-white Construct, where Morpheus reframes 'real' as signals the brain reads, shows him the Twentieth-Century world as the Matrix and the ruined world of today as 'the desert of the real,' and spirals their viewpoint down to a scorched lake bed while recounting mankind's birth of A.I., the scorched sky, and the resulting dependence on machines. The feed then runs through the fetus fields, where a thresher-like farm machine plucks a fetus from its placenta-like husk, and through a power plant where a tiny newborn suckles its feed tube — Morpheus explaining that humans are grown, not born, and that he only believed the truth once he saw the efficiency. Back in the Construct he clicks off the television, defines the Matrix as control, and holds up a coppertop battery as the symbol of what humans are reduced to. Neo shouts that it is not possible and demands to be let out; Morpheus refuses. Neo then tears free on the main deck as Trinity unlocks the cable, Dozer holds him still, and Cypher announces that he is going to pop.

arm-B.summary: Morpheus leads Neo off the main deck of the Nebuchadnezzar into the Construct and, rather than defining the Matrix in words, jacks him in and shows him. Across the loading program, the televised history of the scorched sky, the fetus fields, and the power plant, Morpheus lays out how humanity was reduced to a grown power source, holding up a coppertop battery as the final proof. Neo refuses every step of it and demands to be let out; back on the main deck his body rejects what he has been shown, and after the cable is pulled he vomits and collapses unconscious.

arm-A.title: The Prophecy and the First of the Crew
arm-A.summary: Morpheus answers Neo's grief at there being no return with a myth: he confesses to breaking the rule against freeing older minds, recounts the prophecy of the One and that Zion is the last human city near the earth's core, and declares the search is over before committing Neo to his training. The fluorescent light sticks flicker on, ending the darkness aboard the Nebuchadnezzar. Tank then arrives as Neo's operator, shaking his hand and, when Neo notices the missing jacks, explaining that he and Dozer are born free, genuine children of Zion, before pivoting to the work ahead.

Pleased but disciplined, Morpheus reframes himself as only a guide who can show the door, places the responsibility for stepping through on Neo, and orders Tank to load the jump program.

arm-A.title: The Jump
arm-A.summary: The crew relocates from the hovercraft to the main deck to watch on the monitors as Neo attempts the jump. Morpheus demonstrates the leap across the rooftop gap, then instructs Neo to let go of fear, doubt, and disbelief. Neo steels himself and launches but comes up drastically short, plummeting until the ground gives way like a trapeze net. Tank eases the plug out of the injured Neo, who spits blood into his own hand and asks whether death in the Matrix means death in the real world; Morpheus answers that the body cannot live without the mind. Mouse raises the possibility that Neo might succeed, but Switch and Apoc shut down the search for meaning in the failure, and Trinity, having willed Neo across the gap, departs before Cypher's needling reaches her.
arm-A.action: Morpheus crosses the rooftop gap by leaping it, then orders the next exercise and tells Neo to release fear, doubt, and disbelief. Neo runs at the edge, launches, and falls short, plummeting to the ground below. Morpheus helps him up and draws the reason for the failure from him. On the main deck the crew watches the attempt on the screen; Tank eases the plug out of the injured Neo, who spits blood and asks whether death in the Matrix means death in the real world, and Morpheus states the rule that the body cannot live without the mind. Mouse pushes his what-if about Neo succeeding against two dismissals, Switch refuses the failure any meaning, and Trinity, after willing Neo across the gap, leaves before Cypher's remark to her back.
